newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn gives no further statements on dollar's rise.
newsitem.headline: Bonn gives no further statements on dollar's rise.

text.p: The German Finance Ministry said on Wednesday it had nothing to add to the recent G7 statement calling for an end to the dollar's rise, but fell short of denying reports it welcomed further strengthening against the mark.

Finance ministry and central bank sources said they welcomed a rise in the dollar to 1.70 to 1.75 marks to lower the price of German exports and boost the country's sluggish economy, according to new agency reports.
In early European trade on Thursday, the dollar rose to 1.69 marks, its highest level since April 1994, fuelled by the report about German officials welcoming even higher levels.
It rose to 1.6910 marks before slipping back to 1.6880 by 0830 GMT. The dollar has appreciated almost 25 percent against the mark since slumping in April 1995 to 1.3440 marks.
On Saturday, G7 finance ministers in Berlin issued a joint statement saying they believed "the major misalignments in exchange markets noted in our April 1995 communique have been corrected."
On the same day, German Finance Minister Theo Waigel and Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said they were "satisfied" with the dollar's rate against the mark.
